method:
Manual: Individual young plants can be hand pulled, but older plants develop a deep taproot that makes this not effective.
Mechanical: Repeated mowing can suppress populations but will not fully control them. May be used in combination with herbicide for best control.
Cultural: Burning can be used to remove dead plant material and stimulate plant growth for follow-up with herbicide. Burning alone without herbicide use is not effective at controlling lespedeza, unless done in late summer (when burning conditions are difficult due to high moisture levels). Lespedeza responds positively to burning.
Chemical: Spray plants with a foliar herbicide mix (either a broadcast or spot spray mix) as follows with a surfactant added:
Spot treat with 0.4% by volume of Pasturegard HL (triclopyr + fluroxypyr)
Spot treat with or 1.5-2% by volume of a Triclopyr product.
(Broadcast spray at either 12-24 oz/acre Pasturegard HL or 16-24 oz/acre Triclopyr.)
Note: 2,4-D and glyphosate are not as effective on this species.
timing:
Manual: Most effective in spring/early summer on seedlings/young plants.
Mechanical: Mow while plants are forming flower buds but before they have seeded (early to mid-summer). Repeat each time plants reach 12-18” in height.
Cultural: Burn whenever conditions are favorable in winter or spring and follow up with herbicide treatment in summer.
Chemical: May be done anytime foliage is present during growing season but may be most effective during flower bud stage.

method: **See treatment options below**
extra_note: Template's Additional Information for yellow groove bamboo: Cut all stems close to the ground, let it regrow all summer, then spray the resprouts in the fall with 1% imazapyr plus ½% non-ionic surfactant (this chemical may injure nearby trees or vegetation); a solution of 2% glyphosate plus ½% non-ionic surfactant is also effective. Repeat annually until the plant is dead. Bamboo stems are chambered, so chemicals are ineffective for cut-stump treatment. Digging up the infestation is the most effective treatment (costly for large infestations). Small, contained infestations can be encircled by a barrier extending 6 to 8 inches into the ground while the plants are cut back continually until the root is dead.
